title: Artemis II Waste Management Public Evidence Reconstruction

scope.purpose: Preserve NASA-reported waste-management facts, chronology, operational responses, uncertainties, and evidence boundaries before MissionLab constructs derived operational threads.

urine_collection.public_description: Orion uses airflow to draw liquid waste away from the crew member and into the waste-management system.
urine_collection.pretreatment: Collected urine is pretreated to inhibit ammonia generation.
urine_collection.storage: Pretreated urine is stored in a dedicated tank.
urine_collection.normal_venting_cadence: NASA describes overboard urine venting as a daily crew activity.

fecal_collection.public_description: Solid waste is collected separately in fecal canisters.
fecal_collection.storage: Fecal canisters remain aboard Orion for later disposal.
fecal_collection.vent_line_relationship: The publicly reported Artemis II urine vent-line issue does not establish a failure of the fecal collection path.

contingency_collection.public_description: Orion carries contingency urine collection devices for use if normal UWMS urine collection is unavailable or restricted.

events.relative_time_description: Ahead of the apogee raise burn during toilet-system checkout.

nasa_reported.crew_action: The crew performed spacecraft configuration activities including a checkout of the toilet system.
nasa_reported.observation: The crew reported a blinking fault light.
nasa_reported.ground_response: Mission Control assessed available data and worked with the crew to troubleshoot the issue.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: A blinking fault light does not identify the failed component.
The public source does not disclose an internal fault code.
The public source does not establish the exact root cause.
The public source does not establish that the complete UWMS was unavailable.
No exact event UTC is assigned because the NASA update provides only relative timing.

events.relative_time_description: Following the proximity operations demonstration and before the crew sleep period described in the April 2 NASA update.

nasa_reported.outcome: Crew and Mission Control restored Orion's toilet to normal operations.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: Successful troubleshooting does not reveal the underlying fault mechanism.
Normal operations restored does not establish which component or procedure corrected the fault.
No repair action should be invented beyond NASA's public description.

events.relative_time_description: NASA reported that controllers vented wastewater overboard overnight before the Flight Day 4 update.
events.system: UWMS urine and wastewater vent path

nasa_reported.planned_activity: Wastewater was vented overboard to create additional capacity in the waste-management system tank.
nasa_reported.observed_outcome: The vent activity ended earlier than expected.
nasa_reported.potential_cause_under_review: Possible ice obstructing the vent line was one hypothesis under evaluation, but NASA also stated teams were reviewing other potential causes.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: Early termination of the vent does not prove complete vent-line blockage.
Possible ice was a working hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.
The wastewater tank was explicitly reported as not full.
The toilet was explicitly reported as operational.
The public source does not provide an exact vent start or stop UTC.

events.relative_time_description: During troubleshooting after the overboard vent activity ended earlier than expected.
events.system: UWMS urine and wastewater vent path

nasa_reported.action: Engineers used vent heaters to melt any potential ice that could be clogging the line.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: Use of heaters does not prove that ice was present.
Use of heaters does not establish successful removal of a blockage.
No internal vent-line pressure, temperature, flow-rate, or heater telemetry is publicly reconstructed here.

events.relative_time_description: During continued vent-line troubleshooting on Flight Day 4.
events.system: Orion attitude and waste-management operational interaction

nasa_reported.action: The spacecraft attitude was adjusted to point the vent toward the Sun.
nasa_reported.purpose: NASA described the Sun-pointing orientation as an action intended to help clear the wastewater vent line.
nasa_reported.trajectory_impact: NASA reported that the associated change in the trajectory-correction schedule did not impact Orion's current trajectory.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: Sun-pointing was a troubleshooting action and does not establish the physical root cause.
The attitude change must not be interpreted as an unplanned trajectory maneuver.
The public source does not disclose detailed thermal predictions or vent-line temperature telemetry.

nasa_reported.crew_instruction: The crew was instructed to use backup collection devices overnight if needed.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: Availability or use of contingency collection devices does not establish complete UWMS failure.
NASA explicitly reported that the toilet remained operational.
The source does not establish whether every crew member actually used a backup collection device.

events.relative_time_description: NASA initial postflight assessment published April 20, 2026.

nasa_reported.public_statement: NASA reported that the team was assessing hardware and gathering data to support the postflight investigation of the urine vent-line issue.

missionlab_interpretation_limits: An ongoing postflight investigation means MissionLab must not assign a final root cause from earlier in-flight hypotheses.
The April 20 assessment does not establish final corrective action.
The April 20 assessment does not establish a confirmed ice blockage.

sequence: Blinking fault light reported by crew
Vent activity ended earlier than expected
Possible ice considered among potential causes
Backup collection devices available if needed
Postflight hardware and data investigation continued
flight_day_4_urine_wastewater_vent_line_.mission_impact_publicly_reported: Operational workarounds and troubleshooting were performed without evidence in the curated source set of mission termination.

reconstructable_from_public_sources: Flight Day 4 wastewater vent operation ending early
not_reconstructable_from_current_public_: Exact failed component for the Flight Day 1 fault indication
Final urine vent-line root cause from the early mission updates
